name: Winifred Osborne
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember practicing a request for better wages into a sink.” Monday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Winifred takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I folded my note asking for a raise into that pocket. Now I have to say the words aloud.
appearance: Winifred has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Winifred takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Winifred carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To ask for the pay rise in person.
family: Taylor Lucas is Winifred’s second cousin. Winifred brings a spare shopping bag. Taylor chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Taylor says, “I earned more in tips last month than my own manager.”
connections: Talia Barclay. A secret second wage and an asking-for-a-raise letter could both come out in the wash.

reactions.response: Winifred sets the coat aside until the owner can identify the crystals privately.

reactions.response: Winifred takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.
